Subject: Redwood evals & model recommendations — next steps

Hi Emma / Tomas —

Thanks again for a great discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps to validate model fit on your use case (customer support summarization + answer generation for regulated finance FAQs):

Recap:
- Primary objective: high factual accuracy on regulatory Q&A, plus concise summaries for agents.
- Data: you mentioned ~6k historical tickets, CSV export available, some PII to be redacted.
- Success criteria: prefer accuracy over style; target >90% factual accuracy on closed-book questions.

Recommended starting models (we discussed trade-offs):
- redwood-34b-chat (best quality / higher cost)
- llama2-13b-chat (good quality / cost-effective)
- redwood-7b-quant (low-cost baseline to validate latency)

What we propose now:
1) Run a customer-specific eval on Redwood using a ~1k sample of your tickets and a held-out 500-item test set.
2) Use our eval harness to run the three model variants above, measuring exact-match / factuality / BERTScore.
3) We'll deliver a benchmark report, prompt set recommendations, and suggested guardrails/filters.

Attachments: eval_instructions.pdf (detailed dataset + CLI instructions), sample_dataset.csv (format example). Please: 1) confirm you can share a 1k sample (redacted), 2) confirm the accuracy metric you prefer (we figure default: weighted factuality 70% + EM 30%).

If that works I'll loop in Dev to schedule the technical kickoff and finalize the Mutual Action Plan.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa — adding technical details so Emma / Tomas know exactly how we'll run the evals.

High-level eval setup on Redwood (customer-specific):
1) Dataset format:
   - CSV with columns: id, prompt, context (optional), reference (expected output).
   - For classification/yes-no questions use: id, prompt, reference, labels (if multi-class).
   - Example attached: sample_dataset.csv (first 5 rows).

2) Prompt sets:
   - We'll provide 3 prompt templates (short answer, extractive + concise summary, multi-turn follow-up prompt).
   - We'll run each model with the same prompt set and temperature=0.0 for deterministic scoring (and a second run at temp=0.7 to sanity-check robustness).

3) Metrics & scoring criteria:
   - Exact Match (EM) for structured answers where applicable.
   - F1 overlap for token-level comparisons (helpful for extractive summaries).
   - BERTScore / BLEURT for semantic similarity when free-form text is allowed.
   - Custom factuality check: we can run a small fact-checker LLM in the loop and produce a factuality score (this is what we suggest weighting higher).
   - Final score = 0.7 * factuality_score + 0.3 * semantic_score (default; adjustable).

4) Running on Redwood (example CLI):
   - redwood auth login --org finservcorp
   - redwood evals create --name "finserv-demo" --dataset gs://finserv-evals/finserv_sample.csv --models redwood-34b-chat,llama2-13b-chat,redwood-7b-quant --prompts gs://finserv-evals/prompts.json --output gs://finserv-evals/results/
   - We'll also run a single-model smoke test in your VPC if you prefer private deployment.

5) Estimated runtime / cost:
   - For 1k examples (deterministic) expect ~2–6 hours depending on batch sizing and model choice.
   - redwood-34b-chat will be the slowest / most expensive; 7b-quant will be fastest and cheapest. We can provide a cost estimate once we know concurrency and whether Dedicated capacity is available.

Next steps from our side: share the eval_instructions.pdf and a sample prompt set. Emma — if you can drop the 1k redacted CSV to the Drive link Marissa shared, we'll queue the run and send a preliminary results ETA (typically 48–72 hours after start).

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
